NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
This bundle is the second small slice of the current-only CLI policy and the gates/query portion of the superseded `C-REVIEW-CURRENT-BOUNDARY-1-217D3F0D` design. The normative source of truth is `spec.xml`; nothing here adds a requirement, and every binding obligation is repeated in the spec's acceptance criteria and scope.
Two audit findings shape the selected-close design. First, the existing evaluator's `isAppliedArchiveBundle` early return means a missing or invalid spec, or a present non-applied status, never reaches validation; the validator must classify the selected directory phase before it reads parsed status. Second, the selected-close verdict consumer never calls the exported validator, so invalid explicit evidence is silently skipped or only its first block runs while the verdict still records `pass`. A direct empty `CloseEvidence` and a whitespace-only direct `Command` are already error-severity `change.close-evidence-incomplete` findings of `validateChangeArtifact` and are answered by calling it. A legacy `<Criterion>` carrying `CloseEvidence`, a `CloseEvidence` nested below its `AC-*`, and a duplicate complete direct `CloseEvidence` block are not detected by the exported validator and require a narrow local evidence-consumption guard in the already-scoped `src/gates/ledger.ts` and its companion test.
The applied Verdict's direct children are its `Finding` and `Ack` nodes plus one `AC-*` evaluation node per close-bound criterion; each evaluation node carries `Exit` and `Result` children (`src/gates/ledger.ts:572-580`, assembled at `:533`). The originating anchor is `C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE`'s `AC-EVALUATED-AT-CLOSE` (`spec.xml:478-497`, task `T-003` at `plan.xml:382-405`); `C-BOUND-VERDICT`'s `spec.xml:1688-1697` is a confirming Assumption that those children remain beside `Finding` and `Ack`, not the originating criterion.
The query repair is small and symmetric: `collectChangeView` currently decides archive phase from an absolute-path `changes/archive` substring, so a project root or bundle path that contains those directory names misclassifies an active bundle. Deriving the phase from the resolved project's bundle path removes the substring dependence without a new export.
The reviewed conceptual diagrams below are explanatory. They are not instructions to introduce new classes. Every binding behaviour is repeated in the spec's acceptance criteria. These project-local Commands use the configured POSIX shell and Bun, with no Windows-runner guarantee or CLI runner change.

Alternatives.Alternative: Expand the shared grammar in `src/artifact/grammar.ts` so `validateChangeArtifact` itself rejects a legacy `CloseEvidence`, a duplicate direct `CloseEvidence`, and nested `CloseEvidence`. Rejected: it grows the agreed four-file slice into a shared-grammar change and its tests, changes the exported contract for every consumer, and risks tightening consumers beyond the selected close. The local guard keeps the change inside `src/gates/ledger.ts` and `src/gates/core.test.ts`.

Add a gate-verdict warning channel so the selected validator can report advisory warnings. Rejected: it requires a new output contract and likely forces the gate command surface into scope beyond the four paths, and the warning families are deliberately advisory and non-refusing.

Use `validateNgraceProject` or enumerate archives to validate the selected record through the whole-project surface. Rejected: the whole-project validator walks active and archive directories and is deliberately opaque on archives; it would re-introduce archive discovery and validate unrelated bundles rather than only the selected record.

Make every warning-severity issue refuse the selected close. Rejected: those choices are deliberately non-refusing, and rejecting them is unrelated to preventing malformed or silently skipped selected evidence.

Rely on the tracked `git diff` alone for archive preservation and bounded writes. Rejected: probing showed a byte edited under `--assume-unchanged` or `--skip-worktree` escapes the tracked diff, and an untracked file escapes it too; the retained instruments read base blob bytes and filesystem bytes directly and inventory every actual archive file by exact path.

Fix only the query classifier and defer the selected-close strictness, or vice versa. Rejected: both defects share one boundary and are small, the policy forbids carrying a known defect forward, and the maintainer authorized this second slice for exactly these two modules.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether the selected-close refusals throw distinct reason tokens or one shared invalid-selected-record reason is plan/implementation detail; the binding requirement is that the write is refused before commands run and the ledger bytes are unchanged or absent.

The exact post-change population of acceptance criteria, close-bound criteria, `CloseEvidence` blocks, and `Command` identities is measured through the shipped parser after implementation; no figure is projected here.

The query repair and the gates repair do not share a new helper. If a shared phase utility were extracted it would create a new export outside the four paths and force a fifth file; the spec keeps the phase decision local to each already-scoped file.

Selected-close refusal scenario. A bundle is created, approved, and applied through the real CLI, then its selected `spec.xml` or `plan.xml` is mutated one input at a time: missing spec, malformed spec XML, wrong root tag, wrapper id not equal to the directory or `--change`, missing required section, empty criterion, explicit incomplete `CloseEvidence`, a legacy `<Criterion>` carrying an explicit `CloseEvidence`, two direct `CloseEvidence` blocks on one `AC-*`, nested `CloseEvidence`, a present non-applied status, missing plan, malformed plan, and plan id mismatch. Each mutation makes `ngrace gate verdict --outcome pass` refuse and leaves `run-ledger.xml` byte-identical (or absent), and exact restoration restores the passing result. A Command that mutates the selected plan bytes during evaluation is refused by the plan-byte snapshot guard. The failing-command control still refuses with an unchanged ledger, and a legitimate `outcome=fail` still records the failed-command evaluations.

Preservation-guard scenario on a disposable copy at base. Guard A (archive): clean baseline exits 0; the own active and archive arrival exits 0; a tracked byte mutation, the same byte mutation under `--assume-unchanged`, the same under `--skip-worktree`, and an extra untracked file under an existing bundle each exit 1 and restore to 0. Guard B (bounded writes): clean and the four declared product writes exit 0; an outside-scope tracked write and that write under `--assume-unchanged` each exit 1 and restore to 0. Both guards compare bytes and identities only; no archive content is parsed or executed.
